hn.originalTitle: Nvidia discusses $2k-per-GPU annual fee for software
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Nvidia discusses $2,000-per-GPU annual fee for software that 'runs agents on AI factories' — details unclear about potential overlaps, firm already charges more than twice that amount for its AI Enterprise software platform | Tom's Hardware

(Image credit: Nvidia presentation) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 13 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google.

Huang discussed the pricing at GTC Berlin on October 22, where the company outlined its broader push to build an AI infrastructure business spanning chips, software and AI-agent security . “Software licensing will become increasingly a major part of our company’s business. The way that we license will be…for example, it’s about $2,000 per GPU per year to run all the software that Nvidia provides that runs agents on these AI factories,” said Huang.

The numbers add up quickly. At $2,000 per GPU each year, Nvidia would bring in $10 billion annually if five million GPUs were covered by paid licenses. Over five years, that would amount to $50 billion, provided customers kept renewing their subscriptions. The catch, however, is that Nvidia has not disclosed how many GPUs could be covered by the proposed $2,000 fee, or whether that’s its standard price. It’s also unclear which software the license would cover, or if there is overlap between products.

The distinction matters because Nvidia already charges for enterprise software. Its AI Enterprise platform is listed at $4,500 per GPU for a one-year subscription. Huang’s reported $2,000 figure is lower, but Nvidia has not confirmed that the two prices cover the same products or licensing terms. It should not be treated as a confirmed price cut.

Jensen’s ~$2,000 per GPU per year in enterprise software deserves more attention. Enterprises deploying AI agents need security, governance and someone accountable for keeping the stack running. My bet: OpenShell becomes the standard security layer for enterprise AI, driving adoption of NVIDIA’s paid software and support. Consider the math. Assume: • 10M eligible enterprise GPUs shipped in a year • 50% paid software attach • $2,000 per GPU annually That’s $10B in annual recurring revenue potential. Keep those subscriptions for five years and you get $50B from a single year’s GPU shipments. Each new year of GPU sales adds another potential stream of sof.

The licensing discussion comes as Nvidia develops more of the infrastructure needed to deploy and manage AI agents in enterprise environments. These systems can use tools, access data, and execute tasks, creating new security and management challenges for businesses running them at scale.

On October 21, Nvidia announced its OpenShell Reference Architecture , a system that combines its Vera Rubin computing infrastructure, Vera CPUs, and BlueField-4 data processing units (DPUs) running Nvidia Sentry. OpenShell provides a secure runtime for AI agents , establishing boundaries around their actions and access to tools and resources. Sentry monitors agent activity independently and can quarantine an agent that attempts to cross those boundaries, according to Nvidia. The architecture is designed to bring security controls into the underlying infrastructure rather than relying solely on safeguards built into an AI model or application.

Nvidia had previously introduced its Open Agent Safety Platform in September. The newer reference architecture builds on that effort, extending the approach to enterprise infrastructure and edge systems.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

Other companies are also incorporating these controls into their products. Anthropic is integrating OpenShell and BlueField hardware with Claude Managed Agents to give businesses additional control over what their AI agents can access inside execution sandboxes. Salesforce has developed a Slack Admin Bridge for OpenShell that lets administrators review agent access requests, approve or reject permissions, and monitor activity directly in Slack.

hn.originalTitle: MCP-warden local credential broker so AI agents never see your secrets
hn.sourceOriginalText:
I got tired of pasting GitHub PATs, Stripe keys and DB passwords into Claude Code / Cursor MCP configs. One prompt injection or a leaked chat and they’re gone. So I built mcp-warden — a local-first credential broker for the Model Context Protocol. How it works: • You store the secret once in the OS keychain • You define scoped presets (e.g. github-read, stripe-charges) • The agent calls high-level tools (proxy_http, ssh_exec, db_query) • mcp-warden injects the credential server-side and returns only the result The agent’s context never contains the secret. Allow-list validation runs before credential injection. Sensitive actions can require approval (desktop notification, TUI, or Telegram). Everything is logged locally. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Cline and any other MCP client. Written in Rust, Apache-2.0, fully local. GitHub: https://github.com/ermoluk/mcp-warden Happy to answer questions about the threat model or how people are currently handling secrets with agents.

hn.originalTitle: How we test LLM serving changes for coding agents, two hours of GPUs per change
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Drinking Our Own Champagne, Part 5: What Does It Take to Grow a Self-Hosted Coding Model From Pilot to Team? - Upbound AI

Platform Community Resources Company Docs Book a demo Sign In Get Started Book a demo Sign In Get Started Dennis Ramdass Principal AI Engineer AI Oct 26, 2026 Oct 26, 2026 Read time: 0 mins Read time: 0 mins Drinking Our Own Champagne, Part 5: What Does It Take to Grow a Self-Hosted Coding Model From Pilot to Team? Share Share Drinking Our Own Champagne, Part 5: What Does It Take to Grow a Self-Hosted Coding Model From Pilot to Team? Drinking Our Own Champagne, Part 5: What Does It Take to Grow a Self-Hosted Coding Model From Pilot to Team? This series is about drinking our own champ.

Interactivity: P90 ≥ 10 tokens/s per user, the speed 90% of streams beat (today’s 12.5 less 20%)

Errors: under 2%, counting the turns a failed conversation never got to send

Evals: a smoke test at this sample size, which blocks a recipe only on a confident fail

Among recipes that pass, the cheapest per session-hour wins.

Each part gets a verdict, pass or fail with its margin, from a 95% interval bootstrapped over the run’s minutes. When that interval crosses the bar, the verdict is too close to call, and a fail is low-confidence. Minutes within one conversation aren’t independent, so the bootstrap overstates our confidence, and we treat close calls as unsettled. A missing measurement never counts as a pass, and latency reads as no data when less than 95% of the planned load went out.

7 recipes, one change each from today’s or SGLang’s

Each candidate changes one thing from today’s recipe, recipe 0, or from the SGLang one, recipe 1, in a few lines of YAML:

today’s recipe: vLLM

The baseline every candidate is measured against

vLLM → SGLang: the image and launch command, same flags

A scheduler that may let short turns through while a long prompt prefills

A nightly SGLang. Every tagged release that splits GLM-5.3 across 2 nodes crashes at startup ( sglang#43580 ), so we ran a nightly and will re-run on the next release.

context 512K → 128K: --max-model-len=131072

Shows what the big context costs. It rejects every request over 128K, so we expected errors. We ran it to see how many, and whether our server-side metrics would show them

2 vLLM copies behind one router: copies: 2 and router: EndpointPicker

Twice the prefill capacity at twice the nodes; one router with a long prefix match keeps each conversation on its cache

Modelplane main, upcoming in v0.6, so both copies share one router. As 2 replicas, each would get its own and conversations would lose their cache. Found #558 and #557 on the way.

prefill/decode on SGLang: mode: PrefillDecode , with a prefill engine and 2 decode copies

Long prefills stop stalling everyone’s streams. Built on recipe 1, with 2 decode copies to match recipe 3’s 4 nodes

Modelplane main, where each deployment brings its own router ( #529 ). Before, an SGLang pair reported ready while turning away every request.

SGLang + HiCache : --enable-hierarchical-cache and its flags, on recipe 1

Heavy users’ long conversations keep their prefix in host RAM instead of being prefilled again

The same nightly, and about 0.8 TiB of pinned host RAM per node

recipe 3’s layout with recipe 5’s engine: 2 SGLang + HiCache copies behind one router

Whether HiCache’s gain holds with 2 copies and a router that keeps each conversation on its cache

The same nightly and host memory as recipe 5, in each copy.

recipe 6 without HiCache: 2 plain SGLang copies behind one router

Whether recipe 6’s gain is SGLang’s or HiCache’s

Our first draft’s SGLang recipe changed 3 things at once, so a win wouldn’t have said which mattered. Recipes 3, 6 and 7 add nodes to see what more capacity buys, and compare with each other at the same cost.

How we measure a recipe

Figure 1: A recipe run, from pre-flight to promote or roll back.

A classic canary sends a slice of real traffic to the new version beside the old, which takes 2 recipes’ worth of GPUs, the thing we’re short of. Our rig instead runs the whole recipe on its own nodes, or in a window outside peak usage, and replays agent traffic against it. Each recipe gets one recipe run, end to end in CI:

Catches what’s broken before any load: a deployment that didn’t take, the wrong recipe live, or a fault in the rig itself.

A few samples each of tool calling, a custom Crossplane benchmark and long-context read-back. They block a recipe only on a confident failure.

喝我們自己的香檳，第 5 部分：如何將自架編碼模型從試點發展為團隊？ - Upbound AI Platform 社群資源 公司文件 預約示範 登入 開始 預約示範 登入 開始使用 Dennis Ramdass 首席 AI 工程師 AI 2026 年 10 月 26 日 2026 年 10 月 26 日 閱讀時間：0 分鐘 閱讀時間：0 分鐘 喝我們自己的香檳版代管設計喝我們自己的香檳，第 5 部分：如何將自架編碼模型從試點發展為團隊？分享 分享 喝我們自己的香檳，第 5 部分：如何將自架編碼模型從試點發展為團隊？喝我們自己的香檳，第 5 部分：如何將自架編碼模型從試點發展為團隊？這個系列是關於喝我們自己的冠軍。互動性：每個使用者 P90 ≥ 10 個令牌/秒，速度 90% 的流擊敗（今天的 12.5 減去 20%） 錯誤：低於 2%，計算失敗的對話從未發送的輪數 評估：在此樣本大小的冒煙測試，僅在確信失敗時阻止配方 在通過小時的配方中獲勝，每會話最便宜的獲勝。每個部分都會從運行分鐘內引導的 95% 間隔中獲得一個結論，通過或失敗及其餘量。當該區間越過界線時，結論就太接近了，無法判定，而失敗則表示信心不足。

一次談話中的分鐘數並不是獨立的，因此引導程式誇大了我們的信心，我們將千鈞一髮視為尚未解決。缺少的測量永遠不會被視為通過，並且當計劃負載的完成率低於 95% 時，延遲會讀取為無資料。 7 个菜谱，每个菜谱都与今天或 SGLang 的菜谱有所不同 每个候选者在几行 YAML 中从今天的菜谱（菜谱 0）或 SGLang 菜谱 1（菜谱 1）中更改一件事： 今天的菜谱：vLLM 每个候选者都根据 vLLM 进行衡量的基线 → SGLang：图像和启动命令，相同的标志一個調度程序，可以讓短的輪流通過，同時預先填充一個長的提示 每晚 SGLang。每个将 GLM-5.3 拆分到 2 个节点的标记版本都会在启动时崩溃 ( sglang#43580 )，因此我们每晚运行一次，并将在下一个版本中重新运行。 context 512K → 128K: --max-model-len=131072 顯示大上下文的成本。它拒絕每個超過 128K 的請求，因此我們預計會出現錯誤。我们运行它来查看有多少个，以及我们的服务器端指标是否会向他们显示一个路由器后面的 2 个 vLLM 副本：副本：2 和路由器：EndpointPicker 节点的两倍预填充容量的两倍；一个具有长前缀匹配的路由器将每个会话保存在其缓存 Modelplane main 上（即将在 v0.6 中推出），因此两个副本共享一个路由器。作為 2 個副本，每個副本都會獲得自己的副本，並且對話將丟失其快取。途中發現#558 和#557。

SGLang 上的預先填充/解碼：模式： PrefillDecode ，帶有預填充引擎和 2 個解碼副本 長預填充不會拖延每個人的串流。基於方案 1 構建，具有 2 個解碼副本以匹配方案 3 的 4 個節點 Modelplane 主模型，其中每個部署都帶有自己的路由器 (#529)。之前，SGLang 對報告就緒，同時拒絕每個請求。 SGLang + HiCache : --enable-hierarchical-cache 及其標誌，關於配方 1 重度用戶的長對話將其前綴保留在主機 RAM 中，而不是再次預填充 同樣的每晚，每個節點固定主機 RAM 大約 0.8 TiB 配方 3 的佈局與配方 5 的引擎：在一個路由器個副本和一個將每個對話保留在其快取上的路由器上 同樣的每晚和主機內存為配方 5，在每個副本中。沒有 HiCache 的配方 6：一個路由器後面有 2 個普通的 SGLang 副本 配方 6 的增益是 SGLang 還是 HiCache 的 我們初稿的 SGLang 配方同時改變了 3 件事，所以勝利不會說明哪個重要。方案 3、6 和 7 增加節點來查看更多容量購買什麼，並在相同成本下相互比較。我們如何衡量配方 圖 1：配方運行，從飛行前到升級或回滾。經典的金絲雀會在舊版本旁邊發送一部分真實流量到新版本，這需要 2 個配方的 GPU，而這正是我們所缺少的。

相反，我們的設備在其自己的節點上或在高峰使用之外的視窗中運行整個配方，並針對它重播代理流量。每個配方都會在 CI 中端到端地運行一個配方：捕獲任何負載之前損壞的內容：未進行的部署、錯誤的配方或設備本身的故障。每個工具呼叫、自訂 Crossplane 基準測試和長上下文回讀都有一些範例。他們只有在確信失敗時才會阻止食譜。 AgentX tra

hn.originalTitle: Using thousands of AI agents to uncover new leads in biological data
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Comment 1: The problem was never generating leads. The bottleneck is validated results. It’s performing clinical trials proving efficacy. And this is where I think AI will have the biggest impact—-helping scientist, navigate study complexity and regulatory burden

Comment 2: If you can increase the fidelity of your research model (in-silico, murine, etc) to real life humans then there are fewer false leads.

Comment 3: Drug design is hard because it’s a system problem not a molecule-protein interaction problem. At one point the gold standard for generating leads was using combinatorial chemistry to experimentally screen through millions of compounds. I’m not sure how wide-spread that is any more; it used a lot of reagents. And it ran into the real bottleneck: lead generation tells you little to nothing about the efficacy, toxicity, and side effects of a drug or biologic in actual humans. In silicon will never do a better job at lead generation than combinatorial chemistry. It could help with the real bottleneck. But… there just isn’t a lot of high quality training data on this. They’ve been pushing ML approaches to drug design since at least the early 2010s. The approach has evolved with the trends in ML. Overall, I think the results have been very mixed; much like the traditional pharma pipeline.

Comment 4: > At one point the gold standard for generating leads was using combinatorial chemistry to experimentally screen through millions of compounds. I don't think this was ever the gold standard. I mean, some companies did employ these approaches, but they were generally viewed as low-quality, brute-force approaches (at least at the handful of companies I was associated with).

hn.sourceOriginalText:
Multi-agent LLM coordination in Pokémon · Oliver Grabner

Multi-agent LLM coordination in a Pokémon 2v2 environment

Watch a battle with team chat ↗

The future is in LLM collaborations, and it is important to be able to understand how good agents are at working together, communicating and negotiating actions. Most multi-agent research is about workflows, where agents pass tasks down a pipeline ( Hong et al., 2024 ; Qian et al., 2024 ). To test this, I built a multi-agent environment on Pokémon Showdown's 2v2 format to evaluate these abilities.

"Both opps are Water types … so my Fire moves are resisted on both. … I plan to Wisp Dondozo … can you open with Fake Out to flinch one of them this turn?"

"Good call on Wisp-ing Dondozo. Quick correction though - Fighting isn't actually resisted by Water or Ground, so my Close Combat is neutral (1x) on both. … Locking in Fake Out → Whiscash."

Pokémon doubles is a game-theory environment without full information. The opponents' sets are hidden and damage is random, so winning takes real strategy: reading the other team, splitting targets and planning around your partner. Recent work like the PokéAgent Challenge ( Karten et al., 2026 ) benchmarks Pokémon battling, but each side is played by a single agent, and specialist RL agents still outplay general LLMs there. It doesn't test teammates who have to coordinate.

The goal is a controlled environment where I can measure how LLM agents coordinate, and that can later be used to train them with RL to encourage these collaborative behaviors.

The official Pokémon Showdown simulator, wrapped as a Gym-style environment. Four players each control one Pokémon from a team of three, two per side.

Each turn, an agent reads a plain-English summary of the battle and a numbered list of its legal moves. It can say a private message to its partner or choose a move, and once it chooses, its partner is told what it picked.

Free talk (keep talking until both have chosen), one message each, no talk, and one model controlling both Pokémon.

Qwen3.8-27B plays both teammates against a scripted max-damage bot. Battles are seeded and every team draw is played from both sides, so each talk mode faces exactly the same battles.

Talking helps. Teammates who could talk freely won 64% of their battles against the max-damage bot, while teammates who couldn't talk at all won 42%. Even a single message each (52%) beat no talk. One model controlling both Pokémon (54%) did better than no talk but worse than two agents talking freely, so I think the gain comes from the conversation itself, not just from one mind planning both moves.

Talking also costs. Free talk used 978k prompt tokens per battle, 3.8x the 259k of no talk, since every message means another model call that re-reads the battle and the conversation so far.

I also checked that the environment can tell models apart. A Qwen3.8-27B team won 96% of its battles against a team of 2B models and 74% against a team of 9B models, compared with 64% against the max-damage bot. The stronger the opponent, the closer the games, which is what makes the environment usable as a benchmark for comparing models.

I'm separating the effect of talking from the effect of seeing your partner's move. I'm also looking into turning the environment into a benchmark with a leaderboard across models, and using it for RL training to encourage collaborative behaviors.

Through this project I wanted to learn more about agent collaboration and RL environments, and thought I'd share the results! I ran these experiments on Texas A&M's Grace cluster. Thank you to Maria Teleki and to my advisor, Prof. James Caverlee , for the guidance and feedback along the way.

Pokémon 中的多代理 LLM 協調 · Oliver Grabner 在 Pokémon 2v2 環境中進行多代理 LLM 協調 透過團隊聊天觀看戰鬥 ↗ 未來屬於 LLM 協作，能夠了解優秀代理在協同工作、溝通和談判行動方面的表現非常重要。大多數多智能體研究都是關於工作流程的，其中智能體沿著管道傳遞任務（Hong 等人，2024；Qian 等人，2024）。為了測試這一點，我在 Pokémon Showdown 的 2v2 格式上建立了一個多代理環境來評估這些能力。 「兩個對手都是水類型......所以我的火招式在兩者上都受到抵抗。......我計劃 Wisp Dondozo ......你可以在本回合中使用 Fake Out 來嚇退其中一個嗎？」 「對 Wisp-ing Dondozo 來說是個好主意。不過，快速糾正 -戰鬥其實不會被水或地面抵抗，所以我的近戰在兩者上都是中立的（1x）。對手的裝備是隱藏的，傷害是隨機的，所以獲勝需要真正的策略：閱讀其他團隊的訊息，分割目標並圍繞你的伙伴進行計劃。最近的 PokéAgent 挑戰賽（Karten et al., 2026）等工作對 Pokémon 戰鬥進行了基準測試，但每一方都由一名代理進行比賽，並且專業 RL 代理仍然勝過一般的法學碩士。它並不考驗必須協調的隊友。

目標是一個受控環境，我可以在其中測量 LLM 代理如何協調，並且稍後可以使用 RL 來訓練它們以鼓勵這些協作行為。官方的神奇寶貝對決模擬器，包裝為健身房風格的環境。四名玩家每人控制三人隊伍中的一隻神奇寶貝，每方兩隻。每個回合，一名特工都會閱讀一份簡單的英文摘要，以及一份合法行動的編號清單。它可以向其合作夥伴發送私人訊息或選擇採取的行動，一旦選擇，其合作夥伴就會被告知其選擇的內容。自由交談（繼續交談，直到雙方都做出選擇），每人一條訊息，不交談，一個模型控制兩個神奇寶貝。 Qwen3.8-27B 讓兩位隊友對抗腳本化最大的傷害機器人。戰鬥是種子戰，每次抽籤都是雙方進行的，因此每種談話模式都面臨完全相同的戰鬥。說話有幫助。能夠自由交談的隊友在與最大傷害機器人的戰鬥中贏得了 64% 的勝利，而完全不能說話的隊友則贏得了 42%。即使是每人一則訊息（52%）也勝過無話可說。控制兩隻神奇寶貝的一個模型（54%）比不說話要好，但比兩個智能體自由交談要差，所以我認為收益來自於對話本身，而不僅僅是來自於計劃這兩個動作的一個頭腦。說話也是要花錢的。

Free talk 每場戰鬥使用 978k 提示令牌，是 no talk 的 259k 的 3.8 倍，因為每個訊息都意味著另一個模型調用，該模型調用會重新讀取到目前為止的戰鬥和對話。我還檢查了環境可以區分模型。 Qwen3.8-27B 團隊在與 2B 模型團隊的戰鬥中贏得了 96% 的戰鬥，在與 9B 模型團隊的戰鬥中贏得了 74% 的戰鬥，而與最大傷害機器人的戰鬥中則贏得了 64%。對手越強，比賽就越接近，這使得環境可以作為比較模型的基準。我將談話的效果與看到伴侶動作的效果分開。我還在考慮將環境轉變為具有跨模型排行榜的基準，並將其用於 RL 訓練以鼓勵協作行為。透過這個項目，我想了解更多有關代理協作和 RL 環境的信息，並認為我應該分享結果！我在德州農工大學的 Grace 集群上進行了這些實驗。感謝 Maria Teleki 和我的導師 James Caverlee 教授一路以來的指導和回饋。觀戰←回首頁

Nvidia discusses $2,000-per-GPU annual fee for software that 'runs agents on AI factories' — details unclear about potential overlaps, firm already charges more than twice that amount for its AI Enterprise software platform | Tom's Hardware

Huang discussed the pricing at GTC Berlin on October 22, where the company outlined its broader push to build an AI infrastructure business spanning chips, software and AI-agent security . “Software licensing will become increasingly a major part of our company’s business. The way that we license will be…for example, it’s about $2,000 per GPU per year to run all the software that Nvidia provides that runs agents on these AI factories,” said Huang.

The numbers add up quickly. At $2,000 per GPU each year, Nvidia would bring in $10 billion annually if five million GPUs were covered by paid licenses. Over five years, that would amount to $50 billion, provided customers kept renewing their subscriptions. The catch, however, is that Nvidia has not disclosed how many GPUs could be covered by the proposed $2,000 fee, or whether that’s its standard price. It’s also unclear which software the license would cover, or if there is overlap between products.

The distinction matters because Nvidia already charges for enterprise software. Its AI Enterprise platform is listed at $4,500 per GPU for a one-year subscription. Huang’s reported $2,000 figure is lower, but Nvidia has not confirmed that the two prices cover the same products or licensing terms. It should not be treated as a confirmed price cut.

Jensen’s ~$2,000 per GPU per year in enterprise software deserves more attention. Enterprises deploying AI agents need security, governance and someone accountable for keeping the stack running. My bet: OpenShell becomes the standard security layer for enterprise AI, driving adoption of NVIDIA’s paid software and support. Consider the math. Assume: • 10M eligible enterprise GPUs shipped in a year • 50% paid software attach • $2,000 per GPU annually That’s $10B in annual recurring revenue potential. Keep those subscriptions for five years and you get $50B from a single year’s GPU shipments. Each new year of GPU sales adds another potential stream of sof.

The licensing discussion comes as Nvidia develops more of the infrastructure needed to deploy and manage AI agents in enterprise environments. These systems can use tools, access data, and execute tasks, creating new security and management challenges for businesses running them at scale.

On October 21, Nvidia announced its OpenShell Reference Architecture , a system that combines its Vera Rubin computing infrastructure, Vera CPUs, and BlueField-4 data processing units (DPUs) running Nvidia Sentry. OpenShell provides a secure runtime for AI agents , establishing boundaries around their actions and access to tools and resources. Sentry monitors agent activity independently and can quarantine an agent that attempts to cross those boundaries, according to Nvidia. The architecture is designed to bring security controls into the underlying infrastructure rather than relying solely on safeguards built into an AI model or application.

Nvidia had previously introduced its Open Agent Safety Platform in September. The newer reference architecture builds on that effort, extending the approach to enterprise infrastructure and edge systems.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

Other companies are also incorporating these controls into their products. Anthropic is integrating OpenShell and BlueField hardware with Claude Managed Agents to give businesses additional control over what their AI agents can access inside execution sandboxes. Salesforce has developed a Slack Admin Bridge for OpenShell that lets administrators review agent access requests, approve or reject permissions, and monitor activity directly in Slack.

Nvidia 討論了「在 AI 工廠上運行代理」的軟體每 GPU 收取 2,000 美元的年費——潛在重疊的細節尚不清楚，該公司已經為其 AI Enterprise 軟體平台收取了兩倍多的費用 | Tom 的硬體（圖片來源：Nvidia 演示）{alert('鏈接已復制')}).catch(err =>'console." data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 懸停：bg-neutral-100 過渡顏色無下劃線塊光標指針border-0 bg-transparent-full text-left 連結複製" 。上討論了定價，會上該公司概述了其在晶片、軟體和人工智慧代理安全領域建立人工智慧基礎設施業務的更廣泛努力。

黃仁勳表示：「我們的許可方式是…例如，運行 Nvidia 提供的在這些 AI 工廠上運行代理的所有軟體，每年每個 GPU 的費用約為 2,000 美元。這個數字加起來很快。按每個 GPU 每年 2,000 美元計算，如果付費許可涵蓋 500 萬個 GPU，Nvidia 每年將達到 100 億美元的訂收入，那麼訂定五年十億美元。美元的降價不應被視為確實的降價，部署 AI 代理的企業需要安全、治理和負責保持堆疊運作的人員。

我敢打賭：OpenShell 成為企業 AI 的標準安全層，推動 NVIDIA 付費軟體和支援的採用。考慮一下數學。假設： • 一年內出貨 1,000 萬個符合資格的企業 GPU • 附加 50% 的付費軟體 • 每個 GPU 每年 2,000 美元 這意味著年度經常性收入潛力為 100 億美元。將這些訂閱保留五年，您可以從一年的 GPU 出貨量中獲得 500 億美元。每個新年度的 GPU 銷售都會增加另一個潛在的軟體流。此次許可討論正值英偉達開發更多在企業環境中部署和管理人工智慧代理所需的基礎設施之際。這些系統可以使用工具、存取資料和執行任務，為大規模運行它們的企業帶來新的安全和管理挑戰。 10 月 21 日，Nvidia 宣布推出 OpenShell 參考架構，該系統結合了 Vera Rubin 運算基礎架構、Vera CPU 和運行 Nvidia Sentry 的 BlueField-4 資料處理單元 (DPU)。 OpenShell 為 AI 代理程式提供安全的運行時，圍繞其操作以及對工具和資源的存取建立邊界。據 Nvidia 稱，Sentry 獨立監控代理活動，並可以隔離試圖跨越這些邊界的代理。

該架構旨在將安全控制引入底層基礎設施，而不是僅依賴人工智慧模型或應用程式中內建的安全措施。 Nvidia 先前於 9 月推出了開放代理安全平台。新的參考架構建立在這項努力的基礎上，將方法擴展到企業基礎設施和邊緣系統。將 Tom's Hardware 的最佳新聞和深入評論直接發送到您的收件匣。其他公司也將這些控制納入他們的產品中。 Anthropic 正在將 OpenShell 和 BlueField 硬體與 Claude Managed Agents 集成，為企業提供對其 AI 代理可以在執行沙箱內訪問的內容的額外控制。 Salesforce 為 OpenShell 開發了 Slack Admin Bridge，允許管理員審查代理存取請求、批准或拒絕權限以及直接在 Slack 中監控活動。所提出的軟體定價符合黃的更廣泛的論點
